boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named, university-documented places for individual work, computing, tutoring, or quiet study.

cards.title: Electronic Commons Room 506
cards.subtitle: O’Malley Library · open student computer lab
cards.notes: Bring a campus login and use one of the 28 computer stations for software-based work; choose this lab when you need a desktop rather than a laptop seat.
cards.short_summary: A 28-station open computer lab on the library’s fifth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University identifies Electronic Commons Room 506 in O’Malley Library as an open computer lab exclusively for students with 28 computer stations.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Manhattan University Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Open computer lab exclusively for students; check the university’s live LabStats availability tool before heading over.

cards.title: South Computer Room 206
cards.subtitle: O’Malley Library · open student computer lab
cards.notes: Set up for a focused computer session at one of the 38 stations, then use the library setting to continue research between digital tasks.
cards.short_summary: A 38-station student computer lab in O’Malley Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University lists South Computer Room 206 in O’Malley Library as an open computer lab exclusively for students with 38 computer stations.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Manhattan University Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Open computer lab exclusively for students; the university monitors lab usage through LabStats.

cards.entity_name: O’Malley Library First Floor Computer Area
cards.title: O’Malley Library First Floor Computer Area
cards.subtitle: O’Malley Library · open student computer lab
cards.notes: Use this eight-station area for a quick desktop task near the library entrance, then move into the building’s individual or group study areas.
cards.short_summary: A compact first-floor desktop option inside O’Malley Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University lists the O’Malley Library First Floor Computer Area as an open computer lab exclusively for students with eight computer stations.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Manhattan University Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Open computer lab exclusively for students; check availability in the university’s LabStats application.

cards.title: Higgins 402 Open Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Higgins Engineering & Science Center · 40 stations
cards.notes: Choose this 40-station open lab when desktop access is central to your work; it is specifically identified by ITS as an open lab for students.
cards.short_summary: A large, student-only open computer lab in Higgins.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University identifies HIG 402 as a 40-station computer lab used exclusively as an open computer lab for students.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Manhattan University Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Used exclusively as an open computer lab for students; consult the university’s LabStats tool for current computer availability.

cards.title: Thomas Hall Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Thomas Hall 3.11 · Center for Academic Success
cards.notes: Work alongside a peer tutor or plan a small-group session here; the Center for Academic Success identifies this as one of its study-support locations.
cards.short_summary: A Thomas Hall academic-support space for tutoring and small-group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Center for Academic Success lists the Learning Commons in Thomas Hall 3.11 and says its offices offer quiet study with peer tutors or small-group study sessions.
cards.source_title: Center for Academic Success | Manhattan University
cards.access_notes: Manhattan University students may use CAS services; appointments are preferred and walk-ins are welcome when available.

cards.title: Leo Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Leo Hall 117/118 · math and engineering tutoring
cards.notes: Bring a problem set for a tutoring-centered study block in Leo Hall; use the room’s math and engineering academic-support connection when it fits your course.
cards.short_summary: A Leo Hall tutoring location supporting math and engineering work.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University lists the Leo Learning Center in Leo 117/118, and its catalog identifies the Leo location as the math and engineering tutoring center.
cards.source_title: Center for Academic Advising & Academic Success | Manhattan University Catalog
cards.access_notes: CAS services are free for all Manhattan University students; appointments are preferred and walk-ins are welcome when available.

cards.title: Lee Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Lee Hall sixth floor · evening academic support
cards.notes: Plan an evening study session around the Learning Commons’ posted hours and use the peer-tutor setting for focused work or a small-group meeting.
cards.short_summary: A sixth-floor Lee Hall study-support space with evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University lists the Lee Learning Commons on Lee Hall’s sixth floor; CAS says its offices offer quiet study with peer tutors or small-group study sessions.
cards.source_title: Center for Academic Success | Manhattan University
cards.access_notes: Posted CAS hours: Monday–Thursday, 6–9 p.m.; university students can use free CAS services, with appointments preferred.

cards.title: Kelly Commons Fourth-Floor Quiet Rooms
cards.subtitle: Kelly Commons · fourth floor
cards.notes: Use one of the two quiet rooms for a calm independent work block, with loungers and ottomans available when a standard desk setting is not needed.
cards.short_summary: Two quiet rooms designed for studying or pausing between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University says Kelly Commons’ fourth floor has two new quiet rooms with loungers and ottomans and describes them as a peaceful place to study.
cards.source_title: Kelly Commons: New Additions Inspired by You | Manhattan University
cards.access_notes: Located on the fourth floor of Kelly Commons; no reservation or public-access policy is stated on the source page.

cards.title: De La Salle 304 Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: De La Salle Hall · classroom computer lab
cards.notes: Check whether class is in session before using this 34-station room; it can serve as a desktop study option when classroom scheduling leaves it open.
cards.short_summary: A 34-station classroom computer lab usable outside class time.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University lists DLS 304 as a 34-station classroom computer lab and states that classroom labs may be used by students when not being used for class.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Manhattan University Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Students may use classroom computer labs only when the room is not in use for class.

cards.title: Hayden 107 Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Hayden Hall · classroom computer lab
cards.notes: Use the 40-station Hayden lab for computer-based coursework when its class schedule is clear; verify the room is not occupied before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A 40-station classroom computer lab in Hayden Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University lists HAY 107 as a 40-station classroom computer lab and states that classroom labs may be used by students when not being used for class.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Manhattan University Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Students may use classroom computer labs only when the room is not in use for class.
